posts.neutral_rendition:
I consider this a reduction in what I allege is improper extraction, rather than a solution. ZCG/ZCAP has not addressed the issue as I understand it. I claim that over 90% of coinholders oppose how money is spent, including spending at sex conferences where I allege sex workers sold services while representing Zcash. I see this as evidence that ZCG/ZCAP disregards coinholders.

My principle is that there can be no taxation without representation. I regard ZCAP as insular. I allege that hundreds of millions in today’s dollars were spent on ZSAs, that the community rejected them by 90%, and that funding continued anyway. I also allege that members elect themselves and direct block rewards to themselves. I consider that structure immoral for something presented as money. I believe Maxime has documented this alleged extraction and self-interest well.

We want the block subsidy ended, not merely reduced, so that Zcash can be presented as fair money. The original proposal does not resolve our representation objection.

posts.neutral_rendition:
This proposal makes me angry. It extends ZCG’s mandate until 2032 without resolving the issues I raise. ZCG allocated a $455K ZSA grant after the reported 98.6% vote against ZSAs; I regard that as unacceptable spending of coinholders’ money against our interests. Coinholders pay for grants and committee salaries and are end users, so I believe they should control funding.

As Thomas Sowell put it: "It is hard to imagine a more stupid or more dangerous way of making decisions than by putting those decisions in the hands of people who pay no price for being wrong."

I believe no committee, whether elected by ZCAP or coinholders, can prosper. I see ZCG as analogous to central planning in communist regimes and believe it cannot work. My only acceptable solution is to abolish ZCG completely and let the free market handle funding.

posts.neutral_rendition:
I like the direction of this idea, but need more thought and the complete proposal to evaluate it. It addresses some concerns while keeping the program running and might provide a compromise in an escalating governance dispute; I am not certain yet.

Please provide the source for the “90%+” claim. I am also concerned by increasingly frequent descriptions of the treasury as coinholders’ money. I see those as claiming entitlement to others’ funds, resembling the socialist or communist arrangements criticized in the same discussion.

My view is that ZCG owns its allocation because it is provided through a documented, governance-approved part of the protocol. I welcome proposed improvements to Zcash, including governance. Under the current protocol, though, I regard ZCG’s funds as belonging to ZCG, just as miners own the rewards for blocks they produce. For that reason I think describing those funds as “our money” rests on a false premise and weakens the case for reform.

EDIT: I removed my last question after finding the answer.

I disagree that coinholders pay for these grants: I regard miners as paying, under the consensus decision in ZIP 1016, which provides funding until 2028. I claim coinholders did not oppose that allocation and that prior objections concerned ZCG’s structure rather than ZIP 1015/1016. I regard the current opposition as largely concentrated among a small set of corporate participants. I question whether the people described as “coinholders” are in fact miners who would benefit from redirecting the money.

Sowell’s remark concerned American bureaucrats and administrators, and its continuation was: "Know-it-alls in the school system do not lose one dime or one hour’s sleep if their bright ideas turn out to be all wrong, or even disastrous, for the child." I interpret it as about decisions affecting others. Here, because coinholders already earmarked the money for this purpose, I believe the allocation affects only miners.

posts.display_label: Distinguishes responsibility while alleging a grift
posts.neutral_rendition:
Actually, artkor, I think he is right.

https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/nu7-sentiment-polling-results/54756/22

The poll was generally about NU7, and you acknowledged what you described as ZCAP’s failure here:

https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/nu7-sentiment-polling-results/54756/17

I agree with that assessment. I regard ZSAs as a poor proposal and allege that QEDIT promoted them as comparable in importance to Tachyon when they were not. I would go as far as alleging a grift. Core protocol developers nevertheless supported the proposal, which I believe explains its progress.

That does not mean ZCG was corrupt or that anyone should backtrack: ZCG did not act alone and had substantial protocol developer support.

editor_analysis.text: The post’s concession about responsibility is distinct from its accusation against QEDIT; developer support neither establishes the alleged grift nor assigns sole responsibility to ZCG.

posts.display_label: Consultation proposal with pressure and capacity allegations
posts.neutral_rendition:
I say you have not polled coinholders or ZCAP on this change, and I believe this proposal responds to pressure from a small group. Coin-weighted polls measure holdings rather than giving each person one vote. I claim no country lets people vote with their money, whereas Zcash does.

Do not change the arrangement yet. Allow at least a month of community debate and develop governance that does not let a few billionaires decide everything for a human-rights technology. I do not think the current team is equipped to manage this much money. The community has received a windfall; hire people experienced with treasury management at this scale. I allege that self-interested miners are applying pressure and urge you to serve the community instead. This proposal should not proceed until substantially more debate and polling occur.

posts.display_label: Independent-channel defense with personal motive attacks
posts.neutral_rendition:
I regard two governance approaches as a feature. Coinholder voting is weighted by the amount held, not one vote per person. Projects can seek funding through an elected community board or coin-weighted voting, and it is acceptable for those channels to make different choices.

You seek to eliminate the community funding channel and say that is not your employer’s position, while your employer compares ZCG to USAID. Grant-making bodies, like politicians, will sometimes fund things you oppose. I regard attempts to redirect community money through “X post consensus” as taking it improperly, and urge use of existing governance processes.

I also allege that you do not want the world to use Zcash, based on [this post](https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/end-zcg-and-send-its-funds-to-the-nsm/58515/128), and instead want your employer to profit more. People remain free to build and launch Zcash projects without your permission.

editor_analysis.text: The linked post advocates broad adoption. It supplies the author’s policy case, rather than direct evidence of this interlocutor’s alleged motive.
